$about: 2026-08-06, sixth round of the day: the three severe update-path findings logged on 2026-08-04 (UPD-02, UPD-03, UPD-04) re-run against the current tree before anything was changed, on the rule that a finding is open only while it still reproduces. They had not aged the same way. One is still live and is fixed here; one was already closed by PR #16 and is now proved closed rather than assumed; one is closed in the tree and stays open only until the maintainer cuts a release, which no pull request may do. The observations keep the 2026-08-04 round's target label so they supersede those findings on the punch list; each evidence field states exactly which tree the run was executed against.

$elicitation.$why: This corpus measures whether the tooling conforms - gates, manifests, drift counts. No person was prompted in any of these runs and none was meant to be, so it evidences nothing about whether the standard asks anybody anything. It was never labelled that way, which is how 377 green observations came to read as validation of a product whose central promise is being guided.

observations.evidence: Reproduced twice before anything was changed - once by the case's own procedure on the two releases it names, once live against the current tree. (1) The manifest-keyed diff, keyed by kind + id/path exactly as step 2 designated it, between `git show 4b1179d:standard/standard.manifest.json` (1.0.12) and `git show 62a52d0:...` (1.0.13) reported `ADDED: 2` and `REMOVED: 2` - and even those four are an artefact of keying rather than a change: they are the same two `references` doc links (docs/tree/specs.md, docs/tree/docs-decision-records.md), which gained an `id` field the key preferred over `path`. No file entry was added or removed. `CHANGED: 50`, and the only fields differing across all 50 changed entries were `since` and `purpose`. The real delta for the same pair, `git diff --stat 4b1179d..62a52d0 -- standard/ ':!standard/standard.manifest.json'`, was `4 files changed, 47 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)`: SPEC.md, specs/capability-spec.template.md, scripts/self-verify.mjs, and a three-hunk behaviour change in scripts/sprint-guard.mjs. That payload is smaller than the 18 files the case title records, and the difference is not a correction of the original finding: the repository's history was re-authored between the two rounds, so several commits the earlier round measured inside this release now sit after the release commit. The shape being measured - a keyed manifest diff reporting nothing while real files move - is identical. `grep -c sha256` returns 0 on both released manifests, so the designated source could not have seen any of it. (2) Still live today, content hashes notwithstanding: on a copy of the current tree, a simulated next release appending one line each to `specs/capability-spec.template.md`, `.github/workflows/spec-guard.yml` and `AGENTS.md` - three required entries - left `node tools/manifest-hashes.mjs` reporting `0 entries updated`, and the keyed diff of the manifest before and after reported `ADDED: 0 / REMOVED: 0 / CHANGED: 0`. The only line that moved in the entire manifest was `"version"`. The structural reason, measured on the shipped tree: of 82 files, 45 have their content recorded in the manifest and 37 do not, because only `copy` entries carry a `sha256` and `merge`/`fill-from-repo` entries are adapted by design and cannot. Fixed by making step 2 of update-to-version designate the file diff between the two versions' shipped trees (`git diff <current-ref> <target-ref> -- standard/`) as the delta, with the manifest diff demoted to an index of entry-shape changes and the changelog to the prose. Since no tags exist yet, the step also names how to resolve the two refs (`git log --format='%h %s' -- VERSION`, then `git show <commit>:VERSION`), both of which were run against this repository before being written down. It gains a stated partial-delta fallback for when the current version's tree cannot be had, and a matching `Not this` bullet. What is NOT claimed: no agent was driven through a real update end to end this round - that is UPD-01, still `planned`.

Does not reproduce against the current tree. It does still reproduce at the released versions, which is what the 2026-08-04 round measured and declined to assume closed. Historical half, run first: the 1.0.12 payload extracted with `git archive 4b1179d standard/` verifies at `drift 0 - 100% adopted (49/49)`, and the sham update on top of it - `.standards-version` set to 1.0.13, 1.0.13's manifest copied in, zero file changes applied - reported `self-verify: OK - drift 0 - 100% adopted (49/49), compliant with the standard` while its SPEC.md still hashed to 850ca5eba7e4, which is 1.0.12's, against 1.0.13's b4d058bc5431. Current half, the same sham with today's engine: a fixture carrying the released-1.0.13 payload under HEAD's manifest and pin reported `self-verify: drift 10 - 87% adopted (68/78), 0 excepted`, naming `SPEC.md differs from the standard's copy` and `.claude/skills does not match the standard's copy: 1 missing (idea-write/SKILL.md); 17 changed (add-to-backlog/SKILL.md, ...)`; the identical fixture unmutated reports `drift 0 - 100% adopted (78/78)`. Both halves of this case's `then` - a repo one skill short and still carrying the prior version's SPEC.md - are caught. Closed by PR #16's content hashing. A regression test is added here so it stays closed: case 20 of `tools/self-verify-drift-test.mjs` generates the target version's manifest with `tools/manifest-hashes.mjs` from a genuinely newer tree instead of hand-writing a hash, applies none of that tree, and runs `--version <target>` - the exact invocation step 6 nominates - asserting drift +2 over baseline, the named missing and changed members, that the pin check did not fire, and exit 1. Checked adversarially rather than assumed: with `verifyContent` short-circuited to a no-op the new case fails on four of its assertions (`expected the two unapplied copy entries to count: drift 3, got 1`), so it is measuring the fix and not the fixture.

Half of this reproduces and half does not, and the half that remains is not a pull request's to close. The mechanism now exists and works: on a copy of the current tree, deleting `.github/workflows/spec-guard.yml` and recording `{ kind: file, match: .github/workflows/spec-guard.yml, reason: this repo runs the coupling guard from its own CI system, not GitHub Actions }` gives `self-verify: OK - drift 0 - 99% adopted (76/77), 1 excepted` against the same fixture's unmutated `drift 0 - 100% adopted (78/78)` - the exception clears the drift it targets, and costs coverage rather than buying it. The bar this case actually sets is the released version, and that is unchanged: `git show 4b1179d:standard/scripts/self-verify.mjs | grep -ci exception` returns 0, the same at 62a52d0 returns 0, against 27 at HEAD; and the identical exception recorded on the extracted 1.0.12 tree still gives `self-verify: drift 1 - 98% adopted (48/49)`. What closes this case is a release cut carrying the code that is already in the tree, and R18 forbids a pull request from bumping a version - the maintainer cuts every release. Left failing rather than fixed, and rather than relabelled to match work that did land next door.
observations.waiver: Owner-gated, not unbuilt. The exceptions mechanism this case asks for is in the tree and is verified working in the evidence above; what is missing is a released version carrying it, and R18 reserves version bumps to the maintainer. It closes on the next release cut with no further code, and is left open rather than counted as fixed because an adopter on 1.0.12 or 1.0.13 still cannot satisfy step 4 and step 6 at the same time.
